plan.1_where_sign_application_happens: Its own guarded job, before Q01 plausibility, not part of R01 (R01 only bundles reviewed columns; it must not run numerics). Recommended new task UM21-T04 'Apply CORE-11 full-mode signs to the T03 treadmill outputs' (depends on UM21-T03, CORE-11-P-UM21, UM21-E01; Q01 and R01 then depend on it). Not added to the backlog here (minimal edits); coordinator decides. Design: a new thin runner and adapter step that, for each of the 44 T03 records, re-reads the untransformed Streaming.mat channels one recording at a time, calls run_sign_application(mode='full', pilot_record_path=v4 record) with unit IDs equal to the T03 observation IDs, then derives segments and velocities after the hook, and writes rule-B columns plus sign_application.json and sign_review.json to a NEW output root (never overwriting T03). Open mapping risk: T03 observations may not equal the adapter's heel-strike pairs (curated windows). Step 0 is a read-only probe on one record (observation_id/source_start/end only, under 100 MiB) to measure the match. If the adapter or any bound file must change, the v4 pilot is invalid and a v5 re-pilot (7 records, about 8 s, 160 MiB) is needed first. Preferred: put the observation mapping in the new runner, outside the bound set, and verify bindings list before editing anything.
plan.2_profile_ranges: No approved range fits today, so by default every plausibility check is unassessed (state 'unchecked', visible, never pass). The default profile is a tuner draft with no applicability, review or evidence, and is circular for UM21. Plausibility is a separate assessment layer from the structural/time/side/source-fidelity layer (150 inclusive samples, finite, real clock, side and observation lineage). Eligible canonical columns after T04: pelvis tilt, hip and knee angle, and hip/knee/ankle flexion moments (rule B, audited signs). Never passing: ankle angle (zero offset unreviewed, anomalous recording-sides missing), thigh/shank (planar approximations), velocities, powers, joint forces, GRF/CoP (source-only, N and mm), frontal/transverse. A profile for Q01 would be a new reviewed file with population (able-bodied adults), task (level/incline/decline treadmill), units, canonical applicability and evidence per feature, plus a review record. That approval is a scientific choice: see the drafted decision below. Until José answers, Q01 can finish the structural layer and the plausibility layer as all-unchecked.
plan.3_jobs_and_memory: All launcher jobs: one worker, thread env 1, nice 19 / ionice idle, address space 768 MiB (never raised), serial, dry run first, a pilot before the full run of the same bound code, one record at a time. J0 read-only probe (no launcher, AGENTS.md exception): one record, id/start/end columns only, estimate 60-100 MiB peak RSS, record it. J1 T04 pilot: 1 record (AB04/i0, the pelvis-correction case), then 7 seeded records, estimate 150-200 MiB (v4 pilot: 160 MiB on 7 records). J2 T04 full: 44 records in 4 serial batches of 11 as in T03, one record resident at a time, estimate under 250 MiB (T03 largest 245 MiB, readback 183 MiB). J3 Q01 structural + plausibility assessment: reads only needed columns per record (about 30 of 114 columns, 24,000 rows, under 10 MiB of arrays), via assess_observations, one record per pass, estimate under 150 MiB, below the 256 MiB admission estimate; writes one JSON assessment plus a per-observation table under a new root; pilot on one record then 44. Nothing runs until J0, then J1, pass. MATLAB not needed.

q01_coarse_limits_draft.status: DRAFT for review, plan only; nothing computed, no data read, no profile file written. Decision D-UM21-Q01-1 = B (structure plus coarse physical limits, blatant errors only; no literature-fitted ranges).
q01_coarse_limits_draft.principle: Each limit catches an impossible value or a processing error, not an unusual person. Every limit is a failure with observation ID, channel, sample index and reason; a column with no limit stays unchecked (never pass). Limits apply only to channels published by T04 (hook, copied or physics, as logged), per observation. No limit is tuned on this dataset; the pass rate is not used to choose them.

limits.name: Joint angle beyond any human range
limits.what: Any sample of a published hip, knee or ankle sagittal angle outside the textbook end of range widened by 30 degrees (rule B signs: hip flexion +, knee flexion +, ankle dorsiflexion +).

draft_bounds_deg.knee_angle: -30 to +165 (textbook flexion about 135-140, extension 0; knee bent backwards beyond 30 degrees is impossible)

limits.references: Norkin CC, White DJ. Measurement of Joint Motion: A Guide to Goniometry (F.A. Davis). AAOS values are cited through the secondary table in that book (and similar goniometry texts) that reproduces the AAOS norms (Greene WB, Heckman JD, eds., The Clinical Measurement of Joint Motion, AAOS 1994), not through the AAOS book itself, which I did not consult. The textbook end-of-range values above are from memory and NOT checked against the books in this session; the reviewer should confirm them before approval. The 30-degree margin is my choice, stated so it is not mistaken for literature.
limits.note: The ankle zero offset is unreviewed (offsets are reported, never applied), so an ankle pass means only 'not blatantly impossible', and the ankle column keeps its 'zero offset unverified' chip.

limits.name: Angle jump between adjacent samples (wraps and 180 degree offsets)
limits.what: Any published angle (pelvis, hip, knee, ankle, derived segments) changing by more than 30 degrees between adjacent samples of the 150-sample stride, i.e. about 4,000 degrees per second at about 7 ms per sample. Catches +/-180 or 360 wraps and alternate Euler-branch jumps (UM21-C03 episodes).
limits.references: None; a physical argument (no body segment turns that fast in walking). Chosen, not fitted. The 30 degree value is a proposal for review.
limits.note: The AB07/i10 right-ankle stretch is already handled by D-UM21-C03-2 = C (re-expressed or dropped with a log); this limit is the safety net for anything else.

limits.name: Non-finite published samples
limits.what: Any NaN or infinite sample in a published column of a released observation is reported as 'missing', with the sample index; this is structural, listed here only so it is not mistaken for a plausibility pass.

limits.name: Impossible stride time
limits.what: Stride duration (source frames / 100 Hz) outside 0.4 to 2.5 s, the repository's own gait segmentation limits (contributor_tools/CLAUDE.md, min_stride_duration_s 0.4, max 2.5).
limits.note: The released 7,547 strides already satisfy the hook's 50-250 frame rule (0.5-2.5 s), so L3 will not fail any of them by construction. It is a cross-check on clock and frame bookkeeping. The 15 unmapped strides are already left out under D-UM21-T04-2 = A.

t04_v2_changes.implementation: contributor_tools/run_um21_t04_signs.py only; no bound file touched (git status clean for contributor_tools/common, adapters and run_core11_um21_pilot.py). settle_recording now: hook rule; copy rule; physics rule for power; physics cross-check of hook or copied power (a contradiction at |r| >= 0.9 holds both and flags). r per leg is logged for every power channel (recording_rule.decisions[ch].physics and summary power_correlations). t04_v2_changes.physics_method: Per leg and recording: pooled Pearson r over all finite samples of all strides on the 150-sample grid between SOURCE power and (published moment x d(published angle)/dt), derivative by numpy.gradient with spacing stride_duration/149 (the hook's own method); NaN samples (zero fill) are missing in all three; at least 300 finite samples; both legs must have |r| >= 0.9 and the same sign or the channel is held; needs the joint's published moment and angle (both legs, same multiplier).
t04_v2_changes.precedence: both legs hook-published same multiplier: hook; one leg published and the other unsure (no opposing detector sign, no conflict): copied; either disagreement: hold both and flag; no hook sign on either leg (power only): physics.
